case_name: Spencer and Company v State of Mysore and Others
facts: The appellant company are the proprietors of the West End Hotel, Race Course Road, Bangalore.
The premises of the hotel comprises a total extent of 19.43 acres or 11,19,168 sq. ft., out of which the building area is 1,05,683 sq. ft.
The entire vacant land, excluding the built area and appurtenant thereof is being made use of for the beneficial enjoyment of the building in the area as garden and lawns.
A notice was issued to the appellant on March 30, 1966 demanding a sum of Rs. 35,717.20 as tax on vacant land.
issues: The new provision, s. 99(2)(b) of the Corporation Act, introduced by the amending Act is beyond the legislative competence of the State Legislature.
The said provision is violative of the fundamental rights of the petitioners guaranteed u/arts. 14 and 19(1)(f) of the Constitution.
The Corporation has omitted to observe the procedure prescribed by s. 98 of the Corporation Act, and cannot therefore levy the tax.
petitioner_arguments: The tax on vacant land is violative of Art. 14 of the Constitution because it is levied at an average rate without any relation to the actual or potential income of the land.
The manner of determining the market value was discriminatory, and
The classification of vacant land and land' appurtenant to a building is discriminatory.
respondent_arguments: We are unable to hold that the impugned Act is discriminatory.
The scheme of the Act is that the market value of the land is first ascertained and then tax at 0.4 per cent is levied.
court_reasoning: In order to appreciate the other points it is necessary to set out a few facts.
We are unable to agree with him in this respect.
In the context of determining the market value of the land, which has a well-known connotation, the Commissioner is directed to look at the lands in the area of the land which is being assessed.
holding: We are unable to hold that the impugned Act is discriminatory.
The scheme of the Act is that the market value of the land is first ascertained and then tax at 0.4 per cent is levied.
